title: Moronic acid alleviates non-alcoholic fatty liver disease and fibrosis through PPARs-mediated lipidomic reprogramming.
authors: Han, Jinlu; Chen, Jiong; Hu, Hong; Song, Yun; Chen, Mengyan; Zhao, De; Shan, Wen; Zhang, Qinghui; Xu, Ling
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究莫诺酸通过PPARs介导脂质组重编程缓解脂肪肝和纤维化，虽涉及分子对接和动力学模拟，但核心是药物-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与TF-DNA课题关联较弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and its fibrotic progression represent major global health concerns with limited pharmacological interventions. Moronic acid (MA), a natural pentacyclic triterpenoid, has demonstrated anti-inflammatory and metabolic activity, but its role in NAFLD and fibrosis remains unclear. PURPOSE: This study aimed to elucidate the therapeutic potential and mechanism of MA in ameliorating NAFLD and liver fibrosis. METHODS: The therapeutic effects of MA were evaluated in C57BL/6 J mouse models of NAFLD and fibrosis. An integrated multi-omics approach, combining network pharmacology, proteomics, and lipidomics, was used to investigate the underlying mechanism. Direct binding to the identified target, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors (PPARs), and cellular engagement were confirmed by microscale thermophoresis (MST) and Cellular Thermal Shift Assay (CETSA). The dependency on this pathway was genetically validated using siRNA-mediated gene silencing and further confirmed in a 3D human liver organoid model. RESULTS: MA alleviated hepatic steatosis, fibrosis, and metabolic dysregulation in both models. MA activated PPARalpha/beta/gamma, as evidenced by molecular docking, dynamics simulations, and increased hepatic expression. In hepatocytes and hepatic stellate cells, MA reduced lipid accumulation and fibrogenesis, effects reversed by PPAR inhibition. Lipidomic profiling showed that MA upregulated glycerophospholipids and sphingolipids and downregulated glycerolipids, consistent with PPAR-driven lipid remodeling. CONCLUSION: MA exerts therapeutic effects against NAFLD and fibrosis through PPAR activation and lipidomic reprogramming. These findings support the potential of MA as a novel phytotherapeutic agent for metabolic liver disease.
abstract_zh: 背景：非酒精性脂肪性肝病（NAFLD）及其纤维化进展是全球主要的健康问题，目前可用的药物干预措施有限。莫诺酸（MA）是一种天然的五环三萜类化合物，已显示出抗炎和代谢活性，但其在NAFLD和纤维化中的作用仍不清楚。目的：本研究旨在阐明MA在改善NAFLD和肝纤维化中的治疗潜力及其机制。方法：在C57BL/6 J小鼠NAFLD和纤维化模型中评估了MA的治疗效果。采用整合多组学方法，结合网络药理学、蛋白质组学和脂质组学，以研究其潜在机制。通过微量热泳动（MST）和细胞热位移分析（CETSA）确认了与鉴定靶点过氧化物酶体增殖物激活受体（PPARs）的直接结合及细胞层面的相互作用。该通路的依赖性通过siRNA介导的基因沉默进行了遗传学验证，并在3D人肝类器官模型中进一步确认。结果：MA在两种模型中均减轻了肝脂肪变性、纤维化和代谢失调。MA激活了PPARalpha/beta/gamma，这通过分子对接、动力学模拟及肝脏表达增加得到证实。在肝细胞和肝星状细胞中，MA减少了脂质积累和纤维生成，这些效应在PPAR抑制后被逆转。脂质组学分析显示，MA上调了甘油磷脂和鞘脂，下调了甘油酯，这与PPAR驱动的脂质重塑一致。结论：MA通过PPAR激活和脂质组学重编程对NAFLD和纤维化发挥治疗作用。这些发现支持MA作为代谢性肝病的新型植物治疗剂的潜力。
